arxiv-2202-02228.title: Uncertainty in fMRI Functional Networks of Autism Brain Imaging Data
arxiv-2202-02228.creator: Amin Kaveh, Matteo Magnani, Christian Rohner
arxiv-2202-02228.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Amin Kaveh, Matteo Magnani, Christian Rohner. Keywords
Functional Brain Network
\cdot

Uncertainty
\cdot

Probabilistic Network

1
Introduction

Graph analysis of functional neuroimaging data has attained extensive attention during the last decade. Among all functional imaging methods, resting state functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) has had a prominent role not only in identifying the intrinsic organization of the brain, but also in detecting the changes caused by psychiatric disorders. One way of analyzing fMRI data is to transform it into a brain network.

arxiv-2208-12630.title: Generalized and Multiscale Modal Analysis
arxiv-2208-12630.creator: Miguel Alfonso Mendez von Karman Institute for Fluid Dynamics
arxiv-2208-12630.description: Abstract This chapter describes modal decompositions in the framework of matrix factorizations. We highlight the differences between classic space-time decompositions and 2D discrete transforms and discuss the general architecture underpinning any decomposition. This setting is then used to derive simple algorithms that complete any linear decomposition from its spatial or temporal structures (bases).

arxiv-2210-05963.title: A Note on the ”Various Atmospheres over Water Oceans on Terrestrial Planets” with a One-Dimensional Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Model
arxiv-2210-05963.creator: Tetsuya Hara, Anna Suzuki, Masayoshi Kiguchi, Akika Nakamichi
arxiv-2210-05963.description: Abstract It has been investigated the possibility of the various atmospheres over water oceans. We have considered the H 2 atmosphere and He atmosphere concerning to N 2 atmosphere over oceans. One of the main subjects in astrobiology is to estimate the habitable zone.

arxiv-2211-04886.title: ART/ATK: A research platform for assessing and mitigating the sim-to-real gap in robotics and autonomous vehicle engineering
arxiv-2211-04886.creator: Asher Elmquist, Aaron Young, Thomas Hansen, Sriram Ashokkumar, Stefan Caldararu, Abhiraj Dashora, Ishaan Mahajan, Harry Zhang, Luning Fang, He Shen, Xiangru Xu, Radu Serban, Dan Negrut
arxiv-2211-04886.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Asher Elmquist, Aaron Young, Thomas Hansen, Sriram Ashokkumar, Stefan Caldararu, Abhiraj Dashora, Ishaan Mahajan, Harry Zhang, Luning Fang, He Shen, Xiangru Xu, Radu Serban, Dan Negrut. We discuss a platform that has both software and hardware components, and whose purpose is to support research into characterizing and mitigating the sim-to-real gap in robotics and vehicle autonomy engineering.

arxiv-2304-05576.title: Structured Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted THz Communications
arxiv-2304-05576.creator: Fazal-E-Asim, Bruno Sokal, André L. F. de Almeida, Behrooz Makki, Gábor Fodor
arxiv-2304-05576.description: Abstract This paper proposes tensor-based channel estimation for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted communication networks. We exploit the inherent geometrical structure of the Terahertz propagation channel, including the antenna array geometries at the base station, the RIS, and the user equipment to design a tensor-based channel estimator, referred to as the higher-dimensional rank-one approximations (HDR) method.

arxiv-2306-08832.title: Contrasting intra-modal and ranking cross-modal hard negatives to enhance visio-linguistic compositional understanding
arxiv-2306-08832.creator: Le Zhang, Rabiul Awal, Aishwarya Agrawal, Mila - Quebec AI Institute, Université de Montréal, Canada CIFAR AI Chair
arxiv-2306-08832.description: Abstract Vision-Language Models (VLMs), such as CLIP, exhibit strong image-text comprehension abilities, facilitating advances in several downstream tasks such as zero-shot image classification, image-text retrieval, and text-to-image generation. However, the compositional reasoning abilities of existing VLMs remains subpar. The root of this limitation lies in the inadequate alignment between the images and captions in the pretraining datasets.

arxiv-2502-16327.title: Slow magnetic response and associated spin-lattice relaxation dynamics in rare-earth vanadates revealed by AC susceptibility and magnetocaloric methods
arxiv-2502-16327.creator: Yuntian Li, Linda Ye, Mark P. Zic, Arkady Shekhter, Ian R. Fisher
arxiv-2502-16327.description: Abstract This report presents a new technique to probe the quantitative dynamical response of the magnetic field induced heating/cooling process in rare-earth vanadium materials. The approach combines AC magnetic susceptibility and AC caloric measurements to reveal the intrinsic timescale associated with the magnetic relaxation process of rare-earth ions at low temperatures.

arxiv-2505-03977.title: Call for Action: Towards the Next Generation of Symbolic Regression Benchmark
arxiv-2505-03977.creator: Guilherme Seidyo Imai Aldeia, Hengzhe Zhang, Geoffrey Bomarito, Miles Cranmer, Alcides Fonseca, Bogdan Burlacu, William G. La Cava, Fabrício Olivetti de França
arxiv-2505-03977.description: Abstract . Symbolic Regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering interpretable mathematical expressions. However, benchmarking SR methods remains challenging due to the diversity of algorithms, datasets, and evaluation criteria. In this work, we present an updated version of SRBench.

pmc-10537717.title: Targeting Glutamate Neurotoxicity through Dietary Manipulation: Potential Treatment for Migraine
pmc-10537717.creator: Fahimeh Martami, Kathleen F Holton, Roberto Iacone
pmc-10537717.description: Glutamate, the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system, is implicated in both the initiation of migraine as well as central sensitization, which increases the frequency of migraine attacks. Excessive levels of glutamate can lead to excitotoxicity in the nervous system which can disrupt normal neurotransmission and contribute to neuronal injury or death.

pmc-10707510.title: Recent Advances and Future Challenges in Pancreatic Cancer Care: Early Detection, Liquid Biopsies, Precision Medicine and Artificial Intelligence
pmc-10707510.creator: Lois A Daamen, I Quintus Molenaar, Vincent P Groot
pmc-10707510.description: The incidence of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is rising. While surgical techniques and peri-operative care have improved, the overall survival for PDAC remains poor. Thus, novel and bold research initiatives are needed along the spectrum of clinical care, a few of which will be discussed in this article.

pmc-11335356.title: Sublingually administered bacterial lysates: rationale, mechanisms of action and clinical outcomes
pmc-11335356.creator: Fulvio Braido, Giovanni Melioli, Gabriele Nicolini, Melissa Ferraris, Stefano Di Girolamo, Mario Di Gioacchino, Giorgio Walter Canonica
pmc-11335356.description: This review discusses available evidence on the mechanisms of action of bacterial lysates, and the clinical effects of their sublingual administration. Bacterial lysates act through many immunological effects, including dendritic cell activation, modification of circulating lymphocyte subsets and antibody production.

pmc-11351233.title: Oxidative Stress in Transthyretin-Mediated Amyloidosis: An Exploratory Study
pmc-11351233.creator: Marco Fiore, Chiara Cambieri, Laura Libonati, Federica Moret, Edoardo D’Andrea, Maria Grazia Di Certo, Claudio Passananti, Francesca Gabanella, Nicoletta Corbi, Matteo Garibaldi, Cristina Chimenti, Maria Alfarano, Giampiero Ferraguti, Silvia Francati, Maurizio Inghilleri, Marco Ceccanti, Donatella P
pmc-11351233.description: Transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR) is a systemic disease with protein precipitation in many tissues, mainly the peripheral nerve and heart. Both genetic (ATTRv, “v” for variant) and wild-type (ATTRwt) forms are known. Beyond the steric encumbrance, precipitated transthyretin seems to have a toxic effect.

pmc-12469449.title: Exploratory Analysis of Circulating Serum miR-197-3p, miR-1236, and miR-1271 Expression in Early Breast Cancer
pmc-12469449.creator: Burak İlhan, Sibel Kuraş, Berkay Kılıç, Ceren Tilgen Yasasever, Hilal Oğuz Soydinç, Hani Alsaadoni, Gözde Öztan, Arash Adamnejad Ghafour, Muhammed Ucuncu, Enver Kunduz, Süleyman Bademler
pmc-12469449.description: Early detection of breast cancer (BC) remains a challenge despite advances in screening, leading to poor prognosis in late-stage disease. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as promising non-invasive biomarkers for early diagnosis. The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of serum miR-197-3p, miR-1236, and miR-1271 levels in distinguishing BC patients from healthy individuals.

pmc-12550770.title: Addressing the Growing Epidemic of Obesity: Bariatric Surgery or Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease?
pmc-12550770.creator: Himsikhar Khataniar, Hany Habib, Helene Bloom, Kaitlyn Gernhard, Nabeeha Mohyuddin, Nikki Duong
pmc-12550770.description: adults meet the criteria for obesity.2 A parallel rise has occurred in the prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), which has been linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and cardiovascular disease.3 Despite growing awareness, many individuals with obesity and MASLD face challenges in achieving sustained weight reduction and managing comorbid conditions.

pmc-12562102.title: Prevalence and Types of Inappropriate Antibiotics Prescribing Among Dialysis Patients: A Systematic Review
pmc-12562102.creator: Sara Abul-Ola, Reem Alenany, Usman Abubakar, Takahisa Yano
pmc-12562102.description: Background/Objectives: Understanding the patterns of inappropriate antibiotic prescribing is crucial to design antimicrobial stewardship interventions. This systematic review evaluated the prevalence and types of inappropriate antibiotic prescribing among dialysis patients. Methods: Four electronic bibliographic databases including PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL, were searched. Supplementary search was conducted using Google Scholar and by manually checking the reference list of selected studies.

pmc-12830942.title: Research on intelligent pharmacy unmanned delivery vehicle path planning and drug recognition technology based on JPS and RRT algorithms
pmc-12830942.creator: Hengzhe Yue, Kun Cao, Zhaokun Yang, Quntao An, Lizhi Sun
pmc-12830942.description: This paper is set in the context of an intelligent pharmacy working environment, where we optimize the conventional path planning algorithms for existing drug-dispensing robots. By integrating the Jump Point Search algorithm with the Rapidly-exploring Random Tree Star algorithm, we enhance the accuracy of robot navigation and positioning.

pmc-12969693.title: Acute effects of low-dose bisoprolol on lung function and blood pressure in COPD patients
pmc-12969693.creator: Thomas F. Bradbury, Allison Martin, Robert J. Hancox, Catherina L. Chang, Richard Beasley, Jeremy P. Wrobel, Vanessa M. McDonald, Claudia C. Dobler, Ian A. Yang, Claude S. Farah, Belinda Cochrane, Graham S. Hillis, Caroline Polak Scowcroft, Ashutosh Aggarwal, Channa Ranasinha, Shane Galgey, Christin
pmc-12969693.description: Background and objectiveRecent observational data suggest that cardioselective β-blockers like bisoprolol are safe and beneficial for patients with COPD. However, the acute effects of bisoprolol on lung and cardiovascular function in these patients is unclear, a gap that this study aimed to address.

pmc-13111453.title: Efficacy of multiple acupoint stimulation therapies for primary insomnia patients: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13111453.creator: Ying Wang, Hai-Lin Jiang, Jin-Ying Zhao, Ning-Ning Liu, Lin Yi, Ze-Rui Yang, Shu-Ming Zhao, Fu-Chun Wang
pmc-13111453.description: BackgroundPrimary insomnia (PI) is a chronic sleep disorder with a complex pathogenesis, and various treatment options are available. In recent years, multiple acupoint stimulation therapies have gained increasing attention as non-pharmacological interventions. This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to assess the comparative efficacy of different acupoint stimulation therapies for PI.

pmc-13347931.title: ‘Just opt for caesarean section and pick the birthdate’: a qualitative study exploring women’s delivery preferences after caesarean section in urban Tanzania
pmc-13347931.creator: Daudi Gidion, Columba Mbekenga, Miriam Mgonja, Marleen Temmerman, Muzdalifat Abeid
pmc-13347931.description: AbstractObjectivesTo explore perspectives, preferences and decision-making regarding mode of delivery after a previous caesarean section among women in urban Tanzania.DesignA descriptive qualitative study using semi-structured in-depth interviews. Data were analysed using thematic analysis.SettingA private tertiary hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
